content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4 (Lean): evening overtime plus chat deflection lifts 16:15-20:00 service level to 84.0% against an 80% target, for ₹2,925.","why":"Capacity is down on both queues because of absences, mostly bus-strike lateness (payments 19 absences vs a usual 2.6; general 10 vs 2.4). Call volume is not the problem. Doing nothing leaves the window at 75.9%, with payments at 69.4%. P4 cancels payments coaching from 16:15 to 17:30. It moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments from 17:00 to 18:00. It deflects 20% of status and balance enquiries to chat from 17:00 to 20:00. It offers overtime to 5 payments agents from 18:00 to 20:00 and adds a general callback from 18:00 to 19:00. Predicted results are payments 82.8%, general 85.5% and abandons 4.0%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target with no policy violations.","trade_offs":["P3 (₹3,645) adds 0.4 points (84.4%) and cuts abandons to 3.7% vs 4.0%. That is ₹720 more for a marginal gain.","P2 (₹3,105) costs more than P4 and still misses the target at 79.1%, with payments at 76.0% and abandons at 5.7%.","P1 (₹225) is nearly free but makes things worse overall at 72.8%. Payments only reaches 71.1% and general drops to 75.0%.","Risk to general: moving 3 agents to payments still leaves general at 85.5%, comfortably above target."],"watch":"Handle time on general has run 15% above forecast for the last two intervals. If that continues, general's margin after the agent move could shrink. Also confirm that 5 payments agents actually accept the 18:00-20:00 overtime. If fewer accept, payments could fall back below 80%. As strike-delayed agents arrive, staffing may recover, and you may be able to release overtime early."}
